solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Depressed and unwell after his first skiing event

indicators.note: after places the unwell word behind the opening letter of his

parts.note: depressed means down, low in spirits

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word his

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A miserable, poorly skier faces his first race of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The downhill is the Alpine ski race run straight down the steepest course, a standard Winter Games event.

clue.text: Rise lifts one in 24

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifts means the word is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: 24 down is PACK, and a member of a pack is a wolf

explanation.surface: Something rises and lifts one item among twenty-four, a vague tale of hoisting.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare 24 suggests hours, but it points to 24 down. The blog notes the printed clue says only 24, not 24D.
explanation.definitionFit: The flow is the incoming tide, the rise of the sea, as in ebb and flow.

clue.text: Guy cut in after skiers set off — they score heavily

indicators.note: in places the shortened guy inside the rearranged letters
set off suggests letters disturbed and sent scattering into a new order
cut means the word guy loses its final letter

parts.note: the word Guy, before its tail is removed

explanation.surface: Someone pushes in once the skiers have started, yet these competitors win high marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' makes FIRESKATERS, and 'cut' docks the final letter. 'score heavily' is a pun: their blades gouge the ice as well as earning marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaters cutting figures in ice leave deep grooves, a punning sense of scoring alongside winning points.

clue.text: See 3
See 22
Act oddly on stage in rising mud — steer to avoid it?

indicators.note: oddly signals the three letters of act in a strange new order
in puts the stage word inside the turned mud word
in a down clue rising means the word for mud is read upwards

parts.note: mud means dirt
a stage of a journey or race is a leg

explanation.surface: An actor behaves strangely on a stage sunk in rising mud, and a bullock steers clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges the first word and 'rising' turns the mud word to TRID. The definition plays on steer as a young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle grid is a set of bars over a ditch in a road that livestock such as a steer will not cross.

clue.text: Top 2000 in 1 of 4 in 24D

indicators.note: in places the Roman figure inside the playing-card word

parts.note: 24 down is PACK; a pack of cards holds four suits
M is 1000 in Roman numerals, so two of them make 2000

explanation.surface: A cryptic tally of numbers: two thousand inside one of four inside a reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point of a mountain, the very peak.

clue.text: Aim to give up attempt to score at Murrayfield

parts.note: an aim is a goal
to give up a habit is to kick it

explanation.surface: A rugby player aims to stop trying to score in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Murrayfield is the Edinburgh stadium of Scottish rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a kick at the posts is a scoring attempt, a conversion or penalty kick.

clue.text: Each entrant in luge wobbled for about three miles

indicators.note: entrant in tells us the each abbreviation goes into the jumbled sled word
wobbled suggests the letters of luge shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Every competitor in a shaky luge run travels about three miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbled' gives LGUE; 'about three miles' is an old unit of distance, not a stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old measure of distance, roughly three miles.

clue.text: Broadcast covers American's last fall

indicators.note: covers means the scatter word wraps round the final letter

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word American

explanation.surface: A news broadcast reports an American's final fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is a fall of flakes from the sky, so the noun fall can stand for it.

clue.text: Union left at 7, barking final demands

indicators.note: barking, British slang for crazy, signals the letters jumbled

parts.note: 7 down is SUMMIT

explanation.surface: A trade union walks out of the summit, issuing crazy final demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (British slang for mad) jumbles AT and SUMMIT into TIMATUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last set of terms, refused at the cost of action.

clue.text: Web primarily teaches children

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word teaches

parts.note: issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: The internet is mainly what teaches the young these days.
explanation.definitionFit: A web is a fine woven fabric or mesh, and tissue is fine gauzy material, as in a tissue of lies.

clue.text: Fan is miles away for penultimate games

indicators.note: away suggests the letters sent off and scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A supporter travels miles to an away fixture in the knockout rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Semifinals are the matches played immediately before a final, the last-but-one round.

clue.text: Old habits end in tears

indicators.note: in places the purpose word inside the tears word

parts.note: rents are tears or rips in cloth
an end is an aim, a goal

explanation.surface: Long-standing customs ultimately lead to crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, as worn by a monk, and raiment is an archaic word for clothing.

clue.text: Ran into tree first in fall

indicators.note: first says the tree word comes before the encounter word

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
to run into someone is to meet them, past tense met

explanation.surface: Someone ran into a tree in autumn, or while falling.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to drop steeply, a verb synonym of fall.

clue.text: Oscar's specialities — mince pies filled with good stuff

indicators.note: filled with means the scrambled pastry letters hold the other pieces inside
to mince is to chop finely, so the letters are cut up and reordered

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Christmas mince pies packed with tasty filling are someone's speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' turns PIES into EPIS. Oscar is Oscar Wilde, famous for witty one-liners.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was celebrated for short, witty sayings, the kind of pithy quip an epigram is.

clue.text: Bird in Sochi ordered to entertain top Russian leaders

indicators.note: to entertain means the rearranged city letters hold the other pair inside as guests
ordered suggests the letters of Sochi put into a different sequence
leaders asks for the opening letters of top and Russian

explanation.surface: Sochi, host of the 2014 Winter Games, is told to receive senior Russian leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' gives OSICH, which takes in the two leading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird, the biggest living species.

clue.text: Rep makes it 150, securing date in local ground

indicators.note: securing means the Roman numerals hold everything else between them

parts.note: C is 100 and L is 50 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in puts the date abbreviation within the shuffled letters
ground means crushed and reshaped, so the letters of local are reordered

explanation.surface: A sales rep claims 150 deals after landing a date at the local football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' gives OLCAL. 'Rep makes it' is the definition: the thing a sales rep makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesperson phoning or visiting a stranger without an appointment is making an unsolicited sales approach.

clue.text: Long-winded first half of book's boring poetry

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the book fragment goes inside the poetry word

parts.note: poetry is verse

indicators.note: first half of takes the opening two of the four letters of book

explanation.surface: A wordy review: the first half of the book has dull poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose writing uses more words than needed, the same as being wordy or long-winded.

clue.text: He tackles a complex flip with poise in snowboarding event

indicators.note: tackles means the pronoun takes on and surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: the word He taken as written

indicators.note: complex suggests the letters of flip twisted into a tangled order

parts.note: P is the symbol for the poise, a physics unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: A snowboarder attempts a difficult flip gracefully during competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' turns FLIP into LFPI. The poise is a unit of viscosity, symbol P.
explanation.definitionFit: The halfpipe is a U-shaped snow channel where boarders perform tricks, an Olympic event.

clue.text: One of many capsules lost in a swimming pool

indicators.note: in puts the defeat abbreviation inside the scrambled letters
swimming suggests the letters of a pool drifting into a new order

parts.note: L stands for lost, as in a sports results table

explanation.surface: A capsule, maybe a pill, goes missing in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' makes APOOL from A POOL. 'capsules' suggests medicine but means spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the NASA programme whose many command capsules carried astronauts to the Moon.

clue.text: Women go off rock sideways

parts.note: eggs that go off become addled, to addle is to spoil

explanation.surface: Women leave a rock climb by moving sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: To waddle is to walk with a side-to-side swaying gait, like a duck.

clue.text: Typical snow flurries with rime not absent here?

definitions.text: Typical snow flurries with rime not absent here?

indicators.note: flurries suggests the letters blown about like snow into a new order
not says the absent letter is removed from the pool

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letter pool
taken as written, the frost word joins the letter pool
A is an abbreviation for absent, as in a register

explanation.surface: Snow showers and frost are a given at this event, so they are surely present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flurries' rearranges TYPICAL SNOW and RIME, with 'not absent' removing the A (absent). The whole clue doubles as a description of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter Games take place amid snow and frost, so wintry weather is expected at them.

clue.text: Run indoor trips taking in start of bobsleigh tournament

indicators.note: taking in means the shuffled letters hold the opening bobsleigh letter
trips suggests the letters stumbling into a new order
start of asks for the opening letter of the word bobsleigh

explanation.surface: An indoor run trips up a bobsleigh competitor in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' rearranges RUN INDOOR into ROUNDROIN, which takes in B.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a competition format in which every entrant plays every other entrant.

clue.text: Pick out laptop and hard disk used in event?

indicators.note: out means the letter at the top of lap is dropped

parts.note: to pick a string or fruit is to pluck it
the top letter of the word lap, read from inside the single word

explanation.surface: Someone selects a laptop and a hard drive for a computing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laptop' reads as lap-top, the first letter of LAP. 'hard disk' sounds like computing but means the rubber disc of ice hockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is played with a flat, hard rubber disc struck across the ice.

clue.text: Wolves, say, originally played against Cork or not?

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letters of played and against
or not means the letters of or are removed from Cork

explanation.surface: A football side like Wolverhampton Wanderers might have played against Cork, or maybe not.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is also the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wolves is a pack, the collective noun for these hunting animals.

clue.text: Skiing event all fancy entering, some backing off

indicators.note: entering means the reshaped all goes into the shortened word
backing off means the back, or final, letter is taken off the word some
fancy suggests the letters of all dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Every fancy skier enters a race while some retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' makes LAL from ALL, and 'backing off' trims SOME to SOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The slalom is a ski race weaving between gates on a zigzag course.

clue.text: Check battery in genetic unit

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it
a cell is a single battery unit

explanation.surface: Test the battery in a gene-sequencing device.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem cell is an unspecialised biological cell that can develop into other types, a basic building block of tissue.
